speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I understand you are experiencing right groin pain and had an abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision. To begin my assessment, can you tell me exactly how long ago the accident occurred and what specific position your leg was in immediately after the impact?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Tear and Right Hip Fracture. The patient's history of a rear-end collision, immediate onset of bilateral knee pain, and severe right groin pain combined with abnormal leg positioning is highly suggestive of significant traumatic injury to the right knee (likely ACL tear) and a fracture or dislocation of the right hip. Further imaging is required to confirm the extent of the injuries. REQUEST IMAGES: Right Hip X-Ray, Right Knee X-Ray.
